about.title: Hermosa Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Hermosa Beach's compact, walkable streets and beach-town lifestyle mean residents rely daily on everything from e-bikes and surf gear to household appliances and vehicle parts. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the consequences can land someone in urgent care or worse. California's strict liability rules exist for exactly this situation — you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That can mean the maker, the distributor, or even the local retailer who sold it may share responsibility. If you were hurt by a faulty product in Hermosa Beach, holding onto the item exactly as it was at the time of the incident matters. Our team handles product defect cases and can walk you through what comes next.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning electronics or batteries
Lacerations from failed bicycle, e-bike, or scooter parts
Head and spinal injuries from collapsing furniture or equipment
Crush or amputation injuries from defective tools or appliances
Poisoning or chemical burns from mislabeled products
Fractures from failed safety gear or sporting equipment

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters for Your Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Proof
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to show the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused harm. This can streamline what you need to demonstrate compared to a standard negligence claim.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product can potentially be held liable under California's product liability framework. Our team can help identify who may be responsible in your situation.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Because these cases often hinge on the physical condition of the item itself, keeping the product unaltered and unrepaired can be important. We can advise on proper handling and documentation early on.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability rules typically require showing the product was defective — in design, manufacturing, or warning — and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from proving carelessness, which can make certain claims more straightforward.

items.question: I was hurt by a rented e-bike near the Pier — does that count?
items.answer: Rental equipment can potentially fall under product liability if a defect in the bike itself caused the incident, separate from any rider error. We can review the specifics, including who owned, maintained, or supplied the equipment.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without cleaning, repairing, or discarding it. This physical evidence often plays a central role in evaluating a defect claim, so preserving it can matter more than you'd expect.

items.question: How much does it cost to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: There's no cost for a free consultation. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's generally no fee unless you recover compensation.
